entries.name: Camilla Whitcomb
entries.credit: Boston Globe, March 1, 1919, p.8, Suffragettes Leaving Charles St. Jail; reproduced by Alexander Street.
entries.rights: Underlying historical image is public domain in the United States; no claim is made to the copyright of surrounding modern text or page layout.
entries.identity_evidence: The original printed caption lists the women left to right. Subject is second from left. Berry Pottier appears as Betty Pottier in this caption; Jailed for Freedom and the Historical Journal of Massachusetts describe Berry in the same February 1919 Boston imprisonment.

entries.name: Robert Goldstein
entries.credit: Los Angeles Times, June 21, 1918; historical newspaper clipping reproduced by the Boston Globe.
entries.rights: Underlying historical image is public domain in the United States; no claim is made to the copyright of surrounding modern text or page layout.
entries.identity_evidence: Original newspaper caption identifies Robert Goldstein at right as the Spirit of 76 producer leaving county jail, matching the Los Angeles filmmaker imprisoned at McNeil Island. Cropped to the named man at right.

entries.name: Mikal Kudreyko

entries.identity_evidence: Zimmer identifies Mikal Kudreyko under his aliases Peter/Michael Kravchuk. Belarus-born URW secretary arrested at a Detroit picnic in July 1918 and deported on the Buford; all match this record.

entries.name: Frank Shaffer
entries.credit: U.S. National Archives, McNeil Island prisoner photograph, 1920, number 3477; reproduced by HistoryLink.
entries.rights: Underlying 1920 federal prisoner photograph is a U.S. government work; HistoryLink page is CC BY-NC-ND 3.0. The downloaded photograph is reproduced unmodified.
entries.identity_evidence: HistoryLink identifies Frank Shaffer, Washington Bible Student convicted under the Espionage Act for The Finished Mystery, and dates this federal prisoner photo to 1920. The same prosecution and sentence match the database entry.

entries.name: J. Emma Martin
entries.credit: San Quentin prisoner photograph SQ #33756, Department of Corrections Records, F3717, California State Archives; reproduced in The Watchtower, October 2020.
entries.rights: Historical California state prisoner photograph. Precise original creator and publication history are not established; no open-license claim is made. Reproduced unmodified, retaining the printed archive credit.
entries.identity_evidence: The source explicitly identifies the police photograph as Emma Martin and describes the San Bernardino Bible Student prosecution with Hamm, Sonnenburg and Stevens, matching this entry.

entries.identity_evidence: Source caption identifies Ellen on the left with her sister Rebecca; original plaque names Miss Ellen Winsor and Mrs Rebecca Winsor Evans. Crop isolates Rebecca on the right.

entries.name: Katharine Fisher
entries.credit: Historical photograph reproduced by Turning Point Suffragist Memorial, March 2013 suffragist biography.
entries.rights: Historical portrait; precise creator and original publication date are not stated by the source. No open-license claim is made. Reproduced unmodified.
entries.identity_evidence: The page names Katharine Rolston Fisher and describes her National Woman’s Party picketing and Occoquan imprisonment, matching this suffragist entry.

entries.identity_evidence: The printed caption names Hyman Lachowsky. Zimmer connects him to the August 1918 New York leaflet arrest and Abrams free-speech prosecution, matching this entry.
